rows.what_the_ink_shows: Corollaire 2 begins « Si L est ample rel. … S, alors » (crops/49_scan006_L913_hypothesis.png). The next line plainly begins the uncancelled parenthesis « (et alors seult) », followed by φ_L:A—A′ (crops/49_scan006_L913_converse.png); the abbreviated seult is present, with the existing uncertainty about its terminal punctuation sufficient. The continuation reads « morphisme surjectif » and « fidèlement plat », with a small insertion above the intervening wording (crops/49_scan006_L913_surjectivity.png). Thus the converse qualification itself is in the ink, not supplied by the transcription.
rows.note: Preserve the assertion including « et alors seult » and all adequate existing doubt marks. The supplied mathematical correction says that ampleness implies φ_L finite, faithfully flat and surjective; that finiteness is equivalent to χ(L_s)≠0 on all fibres; and that ampleness additionally requires index i(L_s)=0. It cites the inverse line bundle to reject the written converse. This is a correction/refinement of the author’s assertion, not a misreading, and these mathematical claims were not independently proved here.
